p.t: In short
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t:
**Pick one AI chat tool**, ChatGPT or Claude, and use it every day.
Give the AI **real details**: your store platform, your product facts, and the exact problem.

**Check every AI text by hand** before you publish it.
Start with clear prompts, and **ask for three options** instead of one guess.
Before any email work, **check that Klaviyo shows as connected** in Customize > Connectors.
For template work, **connect Klaviyo through its API**, not the Klaviyo MCP connector.
Before you run an unfamiliar agent folder, **run the security check first**, because Full access lets it act without asking you.
When an agent keeps making the same mistake, **ask it to update agents.md** instead of repeating your prompt.
AI answers are only as good as their sources, so **check every list, number and email** before you use it.
Choosing and starting with AI chat tools
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: **ChatGPT** is the most widely used AI chat tool.
An AI chat tool is a program where you type a question and get an answer. ChatGPT works well for writing copy (sales text), finding marketing ideas, explaining concepts and learning new topics.
It is very easy for beginners.
**Claude** is a strong AI chat tool. It is good at long written content, clearly organised answers, analysing information (breaking it down to check it), deep thinking and problem solving.
Choose it when a task needs careful analysis or a clearly organised result.
**Pick one** AI chat tool to start, either ChatGPT or Claude. Use it daily instead of overthinking the choice.
For long, structured prompts (detailed instructions) that analyse customer reviews, Claude tends to do better than ChatGPT.
When the result matters, run the same prompt and inputs (the information you give) in both tools, and **keep the better result**.
Use AI chat as your **first stop** for any store, marketing or business question. Do this before asking a community or a coach. It is available around the clock.
ChatGPT and Gemini (Google's AI chat tool) give equally good brand name suggestions for dropshipping stores.
Dropshipping means selling products you do not keep in stock, because the supplier ships them. **Choose by personal preference** or by current access. The quality does not differ.
The **free version** of ChatGPT has all the functions needed for niche brainstorming. A niche is a narrow market. No paid plan is required. It can expand a broad category into specific product ideas.
The free version of ChatGPT is used to create content outlines and bullet points, **not finished articles**. The output is a starting structure that a person writes out in their own words.
One operator (the person who runs the business) reported that ChatGPT is **free to use**. It keeps earlier conversation context, which means it remembers what was said earlier.
So later requests can build on earlier topics.
Choosing and starting with AI chat tools (continued)
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: ChatGPT Professional cost about **20 dollars per month** at the time of recording (2023). It gives access to browsing (searching the web) and plugins (add-on tools) that can pull data, such as Amazon reviews.
Use the base version when you only need copy made from your own inputs.
The free plan of Claude has a **message limit**. It can cut off a long generation in the middle of the output. This happened when an ebook HTML file (a web-page version of a book) was cut short.
Retry later, or use a paid plan and generate a full ebook in several steps.
Gemini asks for a **login** before it imports files. Attach the competitor video and exported brand data (files with your brand information) from a logged-in account.
File upload in the chat does not work without it.
ChatGPT Playground at platform.openai.com/playground is a free-to-use alternative. Use it when regular ChatGPT sign-up is blocked.
It handles the same text tasks: product descriptions, ad copy, ad strategies, and preset answers (fixed replies) for live chat.
Chat-based research works best with product context. When you ask about any product, **describe your current work first**. For example, say that you run a Shopify store (an online store software).
This gives more relevant output.
On Windows, press **Ctrl+V** to paste a captured screenshot (a picture of your screen) into the Claude chat.
Ctrl+B switched back to the Claude window from the Kalodata tab. Kalodata is a product research tool.
The Claude chat used for product research ran on **Opus 4.8 at High effort**. Opus is one version of the Claude AI. High effort means the AI spends more thinking time per answer.
The setting is shown in the model selector (the menu where you pick the AI version).
Prompting rules and inputs
Giving the AI the right context
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: A large language model (LLM) is the AI that writes text. It answers from its training material (what it learned from).
Always state the **exact sources, definitions and step-by-step method** the AI should follow. Otherwise it falls back on safe, generic answers.
Give the model as much **product information** as possible before you ask for specific outputs.

When you ask AI for help with a store problem, always state the platform (for example Shopify), the **theme** (the design template of your store, for example the Elixir theme), the exact element involved,
and what happens instead. Without this context, the answer will be generic.
When a prompt asks for Amazon listing data (the product page on Amazon), take the title and bullet points from the product's Amazon listing. Then collect **3-5** detailed real customer reviews.
The output quality depends on these inputs, so do not skip them.
Standard ChatGPT ad writing needs the product facts, the problem, the feeling and the benefit in the prompt.
Brand guidelines (rules for your brand's look) given to a chat AI: provide only the cover page as a screenshot and the colour palette. **Do not send the full PDF** (a document file).
The AI may not read PDFs well visually, and too much information can confuse it.
Do not upload more than **two PDF pages** to ChatGPT. Upload only what the AI needs to see, because large PDFs reduce the quality of its output.
A thread is one continuous chat conversation.

ChatGPT keeps earlier messages in the same chat. So follow-up requests can refine earlier output without restating the product or business name. Keep **one chat per topic** so the context stays relevant.
ChatGPT keeps the conversation context. Follow-up requests, such as making text funnier or more emotional, work without repeating the product details.

It is useful for copywriting (writing sales text), ad copy, headlines, product descriptions, bullet points, video captions, brand name ideas, and colour palettes or hex codes (colour codes written as letters

and numbers).
ChatGPT retains context throughout a thread. So you can refer to previous examples and ask for **variations**.
An AI chat assistant works well as a sounding board (someone to think out loud with). Describe your current work and ask for feedback or ideas. This also works through phone voice mode.
For each specific task, **ask the AI to write a detailed prompt for you**, then edit it.
Reusable prompt patterns
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: Use a short, concrete prompt. It names the problem, the goal and **the number of options** you want.

The AI then proposes several solutions instead of one guess. A pattern is a repeatable recipe: state the problem, state the desired outcome, then ask for three options. CSV is a simple spreadsheet file.
Examples: "My export file opens with broken characters; I need a clean CSV for Excel; what are three ways to fix this?" and "My agent keeps skipping the scoring step; I need every candidate scored;
what are three changes I could make to the instructions?"
Beginner prompt for a stuck problem. It asks for options, then for changes to agents.md (a file of standing instructions for the AI), so the problem does not come back:
I am a beginner and I am stuck on this problem: [describe the problem]. I need this solution: [describe the goal]. What are three options you could give me, with the pros and cons of each?
Once I choose one, tell me which lines to add or change in agents.md so the same problem does not happen again.
Regularly put these kinds of prompts to an AI tool, and **tailor the specifics** to the product you sell:

Regularly put these kinds of prompts to an AI tool and tailor the specifics to the product you sell: ask it to break down a dropshipping idea for someone new to the field, ask it to draft a description for a given item,
ask it for five marketing angles worth testing on that product, and ask it why your ads might not be turning visitors into buyers.

The more of these questions you ask, the more helpful the AI becomes for your business.
Using a ready-made prompt from the ready-made prompt collection:

1. Find the prompt that matches your task, for example the one for **store building**.
2. Copy the **complete** prompt, including all instructions and section names.
3. Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude as a **new chat**.

4. Fill every required input: the Amazon listing title and bullets, the product description, and **3-5** detailed customer reviews. Add your brand name and product name where the prompt asks for them.

5. Press send and wait for the **full output**.
6. Use the sections in the **order the prompt generates them**.
Checking generated prompts
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: A generated prompt must make sense before it is run. Read it, check it against your brand and product, and fix anything unclear.
If you are unsure how to phrase a prompt, ask Claude to draft it, then **review the draft** instead of running it blindly.
Dictating (speaking out loud while the computer types) your brand, product and process, and having Claude turn that into a prompt, is faster than typing.
Check that the resulting prompt matches your brand before running it.
Structure for using ChatGPT to generate product page copy:
p.h: Structure for product page and ad prompts

p.t: Structure for using ChatGPT to generate product page copy: 1. Provide product category and name. 2. List product benefits found from competitor research. 3.
Define your role: "You are a professional copywriter. 4. Ask specific question: "Provide a one-line USP for this product that shows the benefit and differentiates from normal [alternative].
Then iterate on the response. 5. For bullet points: "Provide four benefit-driven bullet points (not features) describing what customers will experience when using this product. 6.
For FAQ: "Generate four common questions and answers for our product. 7. For paragraphs: "Provide a two-to-three-line paragraph that describes [specific aspect] in a benefit-driven tone. 8.
For rewrites using another product as reference: "I have this copy for another product [paste example]. Generate similar copy for our product [product name].
ChatGPT retains context throughout the thread, so you can refer to previous examples and ask for variations.
Bottom-of-funnel (BOF) ad prompts. BOF means the last stage, when a buyer is ready to buy. Ask Claude or ChatGPT for **four** testimonial (customer quote), free gift or benefit BOF ad prompts.
You can also ask for primary text variations (different versions of the main ad text) based on your customer research. You can also analyse a competitor ad. This takes about **20 minutes**.
Make me four [testimonial/free gift/benefit] bottom-of-funnel ad prompts for ChatGPT Based on my customer research, make me primary text variations for a BOF ad. What makes this ad work?
Create a prompt so I can make similar ads for my niche.
When giving a generated prompt to an AI, a prompt that asks for an urgency offer (a deal with a deadline) can be built from the product, price point and niche.
Product copy, descriptions and ads
Store copy
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: Shopify Magic is a built-in AI tool (already inside Shopify). It is available in **all plans** for rewriting product copy.
**Highlight text**, click Shopify Magic, and select Rephrase, Extend or Simplify.
ChatGPT is used to generate product page copy, headlines, benefit points, FAQs (questions and answers) and alternative wording for existing copy.
Claude is used to turn copied product data and screenshots into a product page template, product description, testimonials (customer praise), FAQ
and collapsible tab text (text hidden in a box that opens on click). Sonnet 4.6 was the model used.
**Check every output by hand** before publishing, because the model can state things that are not true.
ChatGPT is used to write copy and scripts for the agency and dropshipping business.
This includes cold calling scripts (phone sales scripts), cold emails (unrequested sales emails), ad copy, product descriptions, business names, colour combinations and blog posts.
**Read** any generated copy against your store's facts and offer details before publishing.

Google Docs is the editing stage for AI drafts. Insert a [Product Grid] placeholder (a marker word that stands in for a product list) where the grid will go. This lets the copy be placed above or below it during editing.
Claude MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard that lets AI connect to outside tools) can connect Claude to a Shopify store, so it can read and write store data.
It is used for bulk meta-field updates (changing many hidden page data fields at once) and internal link updates (links between pages on your own store). **Review changes** before they are applied.
Demo product descriptions: **paste the description prompt** into ChatGPT. Attach the AI-generated product image.
Let the AI infer (work out) realistic product details from the picture before you copy the completed description.
**Enter** the full Demo Product Description Prompt, which starts with You are a professional e-commerce copywriter specializing in high conversion Shopify product pages for premium products,
into ChatGPT. Attach an image file you created in Gemini to generate a professional product description.
AI product descriptions from photos were not possible with the ChatGPT version used at the time. Image input (sending pictures) was not allowed.
The workaround (a way around the limit) is to describe the product in text: its features, materials and target customer. Then ask the AI to write the description aimed at that customer.
After an image is uploaded to ChatGPT, the image view shows **Markup**, Comment, Remove BG, Erase, Resize and Describe buttons. These make a small area change more precise than a text-only request.
Ads, offers and strategy
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: ChatGPT can write product descriptions, ad copy and ad strategy ideas for an ecommerce store (an online shop).
It is the main AI writing tool shown here. OpenAI's Playground (a testing page) is an alternative interface.

An AI chat tool can suggest which urgency offer fits a specific product. Give it the product, the price point (the selling price) and the niche. Ask for time-limited offers, such as a free shipping window.
Then **keep only the ideas** that fit the product margin (the profit left after costs).
Connecting Claude to the Facebook ad account lets you ask which campaigns are currently above or below break-even ROAS.
ROAS means return on ad spend, the money earned for each unit spent on ads. Break-even ROAS is the point where ads neither gain nor lose money.
This is a quick way to check what is working, **without reviewing every campaign by hand**.
ChatGPT Professional, with web browsing and a review-reading plugin, can pull customer reviews from a product listing. This helps you find audience language and objections (reasons buyers hesitate).
ChatGPT can generate custom Shopify code (instructions for your store), such as a custom section that adds AI-powered calculators
or widgets (small add-on tools). This includes store locators (maps that find nearby shops) that search by **ZIP code** (the postal code).
Native Shopify, meaning its built-in features, does not include a ZIP code store locator.
GPT Engineer is an open-source AI project (free code that anyone can read and use). It can write full code bases (complete sets of project code) from a prompt.
AI tools can speed up building, but users still need development knowledge to make the output work properly.
AI assistants can build store features from plain text instructions. Someone with development knowledge (coding skills) must **check and fix** the results. The code may not work correctly without it.
Images, voice and transcription
Image tools
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: The image generation layer (the part that makes pictures) of the email stack (the set of tools used for emails) uses Higgsfield or ChatGPT Image 2.
It is optional.

Higgsfield is also listed among the connectors (tools that plug into Claude) in Claude. The others are Klaviyo (email software), Slack (team chat app), Google Drive and Brandfetch (a brand data tool).
The Chrome extension (a small add-on for the Chrome browser) Voice Control for ChatGPT lets you press the **space bar**
and speak your prompt instead of typing it. It speeds up long briefs, such as long product and customer descriptions.
A browser voice-input extension for ChatGPT lets you dictate a prompt with a **hotkey** (a keyboard shortcut) instead of typing it.
This speeds up back-and-forth iteration (repeated rounds of edits) on ad copy when you supply product details.
Dispatch (Beta, a test feature) connects Claude Cowork to the Claude mobile app. Claude Cowork is Claude's task-running mode in the desktop app.
So a running content task can be checked and answered from a phone. Keep Claude open on the laptop while the task runs. Check progress every few minutes on the phone.
Return after **20 to 30 minutes** to edit the finished articles.
Transcription means turning speech into written text.
Grok (X/Twitter's free AI) is used to transcribe long videos and coaching call replays (recordings of coaching calls). It is faster and more reliable than ChatGPT for long-form transcription.
For long transcripts that ChatGPT repeatedly cut off, Grok (grok.com, free) completed the job in a **single pass** (one go). Use it when you need a full, uninterrupted text conversion.
Otter.ai can convert a recorded video or call into a text transcript. **Paste the transcript** into an AI tool for summaries and search.
rev.com is a transcription service used for long recordings. It costs about **$1.25 per minute**. Dictation on your computer (speech typed by the computer) works for short texts.
A recording can be sent for longer material. Older advice from 2020.
Other AI writing and marketing tools
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: copy.ai is an AI copywriting tool. It scans the web for best-performing copywriting.
It provides inspiration for writing ad copy and product descriptions.
Copy.ai is an AI writing tool used to generate ideas and draft product descriptions. It is **not a substitute** for editing and human copywriting. Older advice from 2021.
An AI product-description tool based on GPT-3 (an older AI model) cost **$97 per month**. It offered a seven-day free trial without a credit card.
It produced a unique description in about five seconds per product. Older advice from 2020, so check current pricing.

Only a generic name is given for "An AI Tool for Product Descriptions and More". It was listed in the December 2020 coaching call for generating product copy. No details of the tool or its use are given.
Older advice from 2020.
Grammarly, as a free Chrome plugin, checks grammar, repeated words and writing quality in real time. Use it as you compose emails to suppliers. Available at grammarly.com.

Grammarly flags written copy that can be stated more clearly or succinctly (in fewer words). Its paid version shows more suggestions than the free one. An AI can perform the same tone rewrite on request.
So a separate grammar or tone-checking step is **optional**.
Compose.ai can draft marketing emails for an ecommerce store. It can also write texts and SEO blog articles (articles written to rank in search results).
An agent wrapper for ChatGPT (reworked.ai) is a tool that lets an AI run tasks on its own. It can research a product from its website and write ad copy by itself.
It needs a paid account, an OpenAI API key (a secret code that links your account to OpenAI) and billing details. It charges **per task**. The example of 25 tasks cost about 14 cents.
Setting up an agent-style ad writer
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t:
1. Get a **paid account** for the agent tool.
2. Create an OpenAI API key.

3. Add billing details, since each task is charged.
4. Enter the API key into the agent tool.
Give a goal, such as researching the product from its website and writing an ad with the problem-agitate-solution framework (a three-step ad recipe: name the problem, stir up how it feels,
then offer the fix).
ChatGPT Playground was recommended here as one of four AI tools.

The others are Runway ML, Compose.ai and DALL-E (an AI picture maker). All four were presented as free to use. Free tiers (free levels) and access terms can change. **Verify each platform** before relying on it.
Workflow automation tools, such as n8n or Claude Code (a coding helper that runs on your computer), connect AI assistants and platforms with other software.
**Not every software** has an open API (a public way for other programs to connect). So some connections need a different approach.
Zapier is an automation tool (it links apps automatically). It can connect the AI workflow to other services. It is mentioned as a reason to consider a paid ChatGPT plan.
Zapier connects apps to automate workflows, such as moving generated copy into a spreadsheet.
Google Sheets (Google's online spreadsheet) can integrate with Claude Code via API (a direct connection for programs). For example, it can push updated forecasts (predicted numbers) to new sheets.
The integration is not yet fully reliable. It may require setting up Google APIs manually. **Expect this to improve** significantly.
Claude desktop app, cowork and claude code (continued)
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: Claude desktop app, cowork and claude code
The Claude desktop app (Claude installed on your computer) bundles Chat, Cowork and Claude Code **in one application**.
It is available for macOS and Windows (x64 and arm64 are two types of computer processor). The Claude mobile apps for iOS and Android can be paired with it.
Cowork and Claude Code on the Claude desktop app require the **Claude Pro plan** (a paid subscription).
Sign up for Claude with a **paid plan**, which the stack recommends, before using Claude Cowork.
Alternatives are ChatGPT Codex at chatgpt.com/codex (OpenAI's coding helper) and Claude Code at claude.com/claude-code.

**Download Claude only** from the official claude.com download page. Look-alike sites (fake copies) are used for phishing (tricks that steal your logins). On a Mac, use the Download for macOS button on that page.
**Terminal** (the text command window on your computer) is needed to install and run Claude Code and to run the Claude CLI (the command-line version of Claude).
The check command claude -version confirms the installation.
Claude Cowork is the native desktop app, meaning the app installed on your computer. Older material calls it Cord.
**Use the desktop app**, not the web browser version, to access Opus 4.6 and the large context windows (how much text the AI can keep in view at once) needed for P&L processing (profit
and loss statement work).
**Go through the full guide** once before setting up anything in this email workflow. Then reread the written instructions and follow them step by step, in order.
Cowork
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: Claude Cowork is a project management interface (a workspace for organising tasks) within Claude.

**Create dedicated projects**, manage file folders, set model preferences (choose which AI version to use, for example Opus 4.7), and invoke MCPs (use connector tools) to gather and process brand data.

Model choices noted at different times differ. So use the model the current interface offers:
**Opus 4.6** for Cowork processing of P&L files.
**Opus 4.7** for Brandfetch MCP tasks. It was selected because it was the most powerful model available at the time.
**Opus 4.8 High** shown in the project model selector for the email template workflow.

When you invoke an MCP tool such as Brandfetch, the act without asking toggle (an on/off switch) controls warnings and confirmations. With it **disabled**, all warnings are shown and Claude pauses for review.
With it enabled, the tool runs immediately without stopping.
**Approval mode** is chosen per project, under the model selector. Ask before acting makes Claude pause for approval of each action. Act without asking lets Claude work without pausing.
This is the mode used for the email template setup.
Leave Act without asking **switched off** for Chrome, because the email template workflow does not need browser control.
The project page has a Set up recurring tasks option. It **schedules** repeated work for that project.

After a skill (a saved set of steps Claude follows) is **started from the slash menu** (the list that opens when you type /), Claude asks follow-up questions for each input it needs. Then it builds the templates.
You do not need to type an extra prompt.
If Cowork blocks some commands, **open the Claude Code terminal** and run the command there. This is the backup route for commands Cowork refuses to execute.
Claude code and VS code
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: **Visual Studio Code** (VS Code) is a free IDE (integrated development environment, a coding workspace).
It works with Claude Code for advanced financial forecasting beyond what Cowork can handle.
Claude Code uses a claude.md file, where Codex uses an agents.md file, for the same purpose: **standing instructions** for a folder. Both work in a similar way.

Cowork and ChatGPT Codex perform at roughly the same level for the email workflow. So the choice comes down to **personal comfort**. Claude Code is an acceptable alternative for users who already work in it.
Claude Code file management: use Python (a programming language) to read and write xlsx (Excel files) and csv (simple spreadsheet files) **directly from the project folder**.
This means you do not need to copy and paste. When new files appear in the folder, immediately identify them, add them to DATA_INVENTORY.md (a list file of your data), and surface the top 3 insights.

Setup procedure for Claude Code in VS Code:
1. Download **Visual Studio Code** (free).
2. Open Extensions (the add-on panel) and search for Claude.

3. Install **Claude for VS Code** by Anthropic.
4. Click **Trust Publisher** to allow the extension.

5. Open the Claude website to authorise (approve) your subscription.
6. Create a new folder named Claude_CFO (no symbols).
7. Open the folder in VS Code and select **Trust**.
8. Drag the CFO (chief financial officer) operating prompt MD file (a Markdown text file of instructions) into the project folder.
Connectors and integrations (MCP)
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: A connector is the name for an MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration.
MCP is a standard link that lets Claude read and write to a software tool. Connectors are managed in **Customize > Connectors**.
To add a custom connector, go to Customize > Connectors and choose to add a custom connector. **Enter the name and details** provided for that connector.
After you add it, the connector appears in the list. Examples are Klaviyo, Slack, Google Drive, Higgsfield and Brandfetch. Klaviyo is an email platform that sends emails to your list of people.
Higgsfield is an image generation tool. Brandfetch reads a brand's identity from its website.
Connector tool permissions are set per connector with **Always allow**. This lets a tool run without asking you each time.
The Brandfetch connector offers read-only tools. Read-only tools can look at data but cannot change it. They are Search Brands, Build Logo URLs, Get Brand Details and Get Brand Context.
All of them are set to Always allow.
In Customize > Connectors, Klaviyo is listed under a Not connected heading until you link it. **Check this status** before you start any email work.
Brandfetch MCP reads a brand's own website. It pulls out the brand voice (the tone of its writing), colours, fonts and other identity parts.
These are saved as a brand kit, which is a set of brand style rules. The brand kit is then used to style the universal content blocks, which are reusable pieces of an email layout.
Brandfetch requires a developer account at the Brandfetch developer portal (brandfetch.com). A developer portal is the website where you create the keys a tool needs.
In it, you generate a private API key and a client ID. An API key is a private code that lets a program prove who it is, like a password for software. A client ID is an ID that names your app.
**Install the MCP with that key.** The Pro plan (a paid plan) is recommended for the sign-up.
Klaviyo
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: Klaviyo MCP connects the AI tool to a Klaviyo account.
The AI can read existing data, such as campaigns (one-time email sends) and subscriber information (details about the people on your list). It can also write new email content back into Klaviyo.
Klaviyo requires a private API key. Generate it in the Klaviyo developer portal (developer.klaviyo.com). **Use this key** to connect the AI tool.
**Do not install the Klaviyo MCP connector for the template workflow.** The source calls it flawed and very limiting. It does not allow the template and content block work that is needed.

**Connect Claude to Klaviyo directly through the Klaviyo API** instead. An API (application programming interface) is a way for programs to talk to each other. Use the Python scripts supplied inside the skills.
A skill is a saved set of instructions the AI can run. The API connection is much more capable and covers the full template workflow.
The older setup check still lists the Klaviyo MCP as one of its three checks. If the two disagree, follow the template-workflow instruction for Claude desktop. **Use the API.**
A custom AI assistant is a general LLM (large language model,
p.h: Custom AI assistants and Claude projects: What a custom assistant is

p.t: an AI trained on huge amounts of text) such as Claude or ChatGPT. You load it with your own instructions, product information, templates and step-by-step processes.
At minimum, it can handle any text task. Visuals depend on the platform and the LLM used.
In Claude, a project is a saved workspace. It holds the assistant's instructions and reference files. The instructions say how to create particular ad types or how to research ideas.
The files hold brand-specific information.
The output quality depends on the instructions. **Write a large body of detailed instructions**, based on a proven system. This keeps the output on the right path.
The assistant then produces research documents, scripts and visual assets from the information it was given.
Custom AI assistants and Claude projects: What a custom assistant is (continued)
A generic LLM without brand instructions and files gives generic research. It uses general sources such as platform guidelines or old top search results.
This dilutes your messaging and can lead to a poor creative path.
Example kickoff prompt for a market study. Before you send it, **upload the product description and the brand's internal strategy documents** into the assistant's workspace.
This way the study follows your own methodology, not generic sources. Specify that the results arrive in the layout your templates prescribe.
Hello Magnus. First go through the attached product description, and afterwards run a market study for our label.
Reference files for a Claude project can be uploaded as Markdown (.md) or Word (.docx) files.
Markdown is a plain-text file with simple formatting marks. The file format affects how easily the assistant reads it.
Markdown is generally easier for AI to parse (read and understand), so mixing formats is workable. Plain-text files are still the better default.

The Files panel of a Claude project shows a capacity indicator. Capacity is how much of the project's space is in use, shown as a percentage. In the example, about ten brand files used 15% of capacity.
For the script prompt to produce a usable script, **add five reference files** to the Claude project.

They are a voice guide, a structure library, a banned word list, an avatar (a profile of your ideal customer) and a psychology lens. Without these files, the script stays generic and you must check it by hand.

A workflow is a fixed series of steps that gets a job done.
1. **Describe the outcome you want** in plain language.

2. Ask Claude to design the workflow that achieves it.
3. Ask Claude to build it in the workflow tool or as code.
4. **Check the result manually** for mistakes and holes in the process before you rely on it.
Email AI stack
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: The AI email stack has four layers. A stack is a set of tools that work together.
AI builders for planning and template work: Claude Cowork as the main tool, ChatGPT Codex as an equal alternative, and Claude Code only if you prefer it.
An image generation layer, which is optional. Use Higgsfield or ChatGPT Image 2.
A brand identity layer. Brandfetch MCP extracts brand voice, colours and fonts from a website.
The email platform Klaviyo. Connect it through the Klaviyo MCP, or through the API for the template workflow. This lets data move between the AI tool and your account, in both directions.
The email stack's skills run as slash commands inside Claude Cowork. A slash command is a shortcut you type that starts with /.

/email-template-builder makes reusable blocks.
The email flow builder skill makes flows. A flow is an automatic email sequence that starts from an action.

/email-draft-review checks drafts.
/email-domain-audit checks deliverability, which is whether your emails reach the inbox.
/email-strat-plan plans campaigns.
**Foundation stage first:** install every tool from the bundle zip (a single compressed file that holds all the tools) and set up a working stack. Create a defined folder structure too.

Do this before any email content is built. Nothing else starts until this stage is complete.
Setup verification for the AI email stack in Claude Cowork:

1. Ask Claude Cowork to list your Klaviyo campaigns through the Klaviyo MCP.
2. Ask it to look up your brand domain with Brandfetch.
3. Type /email-template-builder to confirm the template skill is available.
All three checks should respond. **If one fails, fix that tool or connection** before you continue.
AI agent folders (Codex and Claude Code): Concepts and set-up
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: An agent is an AI that can take actions, not only answer.
An agent folder is a folder that holds its instructions.
Codex is a desktop app from ChatGPT that can run agent folders on your computer. As of May 2026, it was recommended for beginners over Claude Code.
The reason is that you link your existing ChatGPT account, and setup is simpler.

Codex and Claude Code can be compared. Claude Code is the folder-instruction tool and uses claude.md. Codex uses agents.md. Both are instruction files. For the email workflow, the two are comparable in level.
The agents.md file is the most important file in an agent folder. It holds the standing instructions that shape how the AI behaves in that folder.
Agent folders can be downloaded from GitHub. GitHub is an online place to store and share folders. Downloading also makes it possible to deploy and update them later.
You then open the downloaded folder locally in Codex.

**Create one dedicated AI folder** on your computer and put agent folders inside it. Anything you drag into that folder structure is visible to the AI. Keep sensitive data, such as credit card details, out of it.
**Keep one master AI folder** on your computer. Place each agent folder inside it as a subfolder. Open each agent folder separately in Codex. Each opening starts its own chat, scoped to that folder.
To connect an agent folder, open Codex and go to File > Open folder. Then select the agent folder. Codex starts a new chat scoped to that folder.

In the Codex chat window, the access setting is at the bottom. **Set it to Full access** so the agent can run without asking you for each action. The model is set to 5.5, with reasoning effort at Extra High.
Reasoning effort is how hard the AI thinks before it answers. Both settings are shown in the same selector.
In the Codex chat box there is a Toggle /Fast option. It makes responses faster. Codex may suggest turning it on based on past use. It increases plan usage.
AI agent folders (Codex and Claude Code): Concepts and set-up (continued)
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: For careful agent work where depth matters more than speed, keep Extra High reasoning.
Review and Undo: after an agent edits files, Codex shows a count such as Edited 3 files, with Undo and Review buttons. Review lists each changed file with its line changes.

For example, +9 -2 means nine lines added and two removed. **Check every change before you keep it.** Use Undo to revert.
First start of a downloaded agent folder:
1. **Download the agent folder**, for example from GitHub. Place it inside your dedicated AI folder.

2. Open Codex and go to File > Open folder. Then select the agent folder.
3. Set access to Full access and the model to 5.5 with Extra High reasoning.
4. **Start a new chat and send the security-check prompt** before anything else runs.
5. Open the handoff document and the startup prompt file yourself and read them, if you want to see them directly. A handoff document is a notes file that explains the setup.

6. Read the agent's explanation of what will happen. Check that it matches what you want.
7. Click go to load the agent and start its workflow.

8. Answer the setup questions the agent asks before it begins searching.
Security-check prompt:
Please explain what is inside this folder and what it is for. It is a project I want to start working on. Check whether anything in it is malicious or could harm my computer or my data.
Then explain step by step what will happen when we start, beginning with an analysis of the handoff document and the startup prompt, so I know what I am agreeing to before anything runs.
Do not change, send, or delete any files yet.

**Do not run an unfamiliar agent folder with Full access** before you check its contents. It can contain malicious instructions or files. Always read the handoff and startup files. Ask the AI to explain the workflow first.
Setup questions and what agents do
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: The agent's setup questions show what it needs before it searches. They ask for the target role or candidate type.
They ask what a strong fit and a disqualifier look like. They ask where proof of work can be found. They ask for example people, companies, websites or keywords to start from.
Clear answers make the first pass more useful.
Recruiting-style agents are built to search public sources only, unless you explicitly approve something else. They add qualified candidates to a tracking CSV, which is a plain spreadsheet file.
Each entry includes evidence, scores, rankings, risks and next steps.
**The agent must not** contact anyone, submit forms, share lists, change permissions or update outside systems. The only exception is an action you explicitly approve.
Ask for this approval in writing for each external step.
**Limit file searches and reads** to the agent folder, unless you explicitly ask for a wider search. Writing this rule into agents.md keeps the agent from browsing unrelated files on your computer.

Files in a recruiting agent folder:
**AGENTS.md**: Standing instructions for the agent: rules, boundaries and how to behave in this folder
**START-HERE-PROMPT.md**: Startup prompt that tells the agent how to begin the workflow
**HANDOFF.md**: Beginner-facing setup and execution guide for the agent kit
**growth-mentor-sourcing.md**: Role-specific sourcing playbook with candidate qualification rules
**role-sourcing-template.md**: Copyable template for creating a new role-specific sourcing playbook
**growth-mentor-candidates.csv**: Working candidate tracker, where qualified people are logged
**starter-candidates.csv**: Starting list of candidates the agent works through first
Getting unstuck and improving agents
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: When an agent keeps giving wrong answers or misunderstands the task,
**change agents.md** instead of repeating your prompt. Ask the agent to update agents.md after each repeated error. Its later answers become more accurate.
Standing safety prompt for a beginner. It also makes the agent keep agents.md up to date:
I am a beginner. Please always run the security checks before doing any work in this folder, and explain each step in simple language.
Add these instructions to agents.md so you follow them in future sessions. Update agents.md whenever the same mistake repeats or when we learn something new in this process.

When you get stuck, **ask the AI first**, before you ask a mentor. For example, ask when a folder asks for an integration that does not exist. Agents can usually propose a workaround or a custom tool.

Example: an agent may report that it cannot push files to Google Drive, because no Google Drive integration exists. Ask the AI how to work around this. One option is saving a local file, then uploading it manually.
Another is building a small custom tool.

An agent folder can be used for YouTube scripts, creative ideas and recruiting. A recruiting scraper (a tool that collects data from websites automatically) can search LinkedIn, YouTube and Twitter for potential clients.
Any agent can be used for a new project, as long as its instructions are set up correctly.
A large language model such as ChatGPT or Claude predicts the most useful next output.
p.h: AI limits and verification: How AI produces answers

p.t: It predicts this from the text it was trained on. It does not produce original insight from nothing. Its answers are only as good as its source material.
AI output quality depends entirely on its training material. If the sources are wrong, outdated or unproven, the answers will be unreliable. This is true even when they sound confident.
When a general AI model draws on many conflicting marketing opinions, it averages them. The result is a watered-down answer that commits to no clear path.
Broad marketing questions with no defined source produce this diluted result.

AI is trained to avoid mistakes. So when it is unsure which source is best, it falls back on safe, generic answers. **Always state the exact sources, definitions and step-by-step method** the AI should follow.
Do not leave this open.
A single trained person can only do one task at a time. Trained AI agents can apply the same proven instructions across many tasks at once.
AI limits and verification: How AI produces answers (continued)
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: This is the main reason to build a repeatable, well-instructed system for AI.
Generative AI works by predictive generation. The model outputs what would be most useful to say next, based on your question and everything it was trained on.
Terms such as predictive modelling describe the same process. A different label does not change how the answer is produced.
Large language models such as ChatGPT and Claude are trained on mixed text. The mix includes books, blogs, essays, forum and social media posts, Wikipedia, and other web pages.
Their answers reflect that mix. So topics with conflicting opinions, like marketing, give inconsistent results.
A model trained only on a 300-year-old science book can answer questions from that book well. It cannot propose new experiments or ideas beyond what the book contains.
Its output is limited to the scope of its training material.
Chat assistants do well on general questions, largely because they can draw on the wider internet. But broad access to sources does not mean the answer is proven for your specific business task.
**Choose the source material for that task deliberately.**
**Check every generated list, email or statement** before you publish it.
AI tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini sometimes produce incorrect answers.
ChatGPT is not reliable for current trend data.

This includes lists of the top dropshipping products (products sold through a store without holding stock) for the coming period, or exact market numbers. **Verify any figures** it gives before you use them.
Use it mainly for text and ideas.
Many prepackaged AI dropshipping tools are thin wrappers. A thin wrapper is a product that only adds a layer on top of a general chat AI such as ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot or Grok.
Such tools are often built on outdated technology. Using the general models directly is usually cheaper and more current.
**Do not use an unfamiliar agent folder with Full access** before checking its contents.
Changing features and limits
p.s: AI assistants and custom AI workflows

p.t: ChatGPT's web browsing was switched off temporarily. Users had found ways to bypass privacy controls through links.
AI tool features such as web search can be removed or changed without notice. **Check current availability** before you build a workflow on them.
Pro plans have character limits. Long documents may need to be shortened.
Four AI tools were recommended as examples: ChatGPT Playground, Runway ML, Compose.ai and DALL-E. They were presented as free to use.
Free tiers and access terms can change, so **verify each platform** before you rely on it.

Free-plan limits and file import rules change over time. Examples are the Gemini login requirement and the Claude free-plan message cap. **Check them on the platform** before you plan a large job around them.
**Download AI apps only from the official site.** Look-alike sites are used for phishing, which is when fake sites steal your logins.
**Limit agent access to the folder you opened**, and keep sensitive data out of any folder the AI can read.

Quick comparison of the two recommended AI chat tools for beginners:
**Ease of use**

ChatGPT: Very beginner friendly
Claude: Also simple
**Best for**

ChatGPT: Marketing, ideas, copywriting
Claude: Deep thinking and structured answers
Both tools are strong enough for store work. **Start using one daily.** The choice matters less than that.
